newsitem.title: USA: Spring municipal elections urged in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Spring municipal elections urged in Bosnia.

text.p: The head of the international mission organising Bosnia's postwar elections said on Friday he hoped municipal elections there would be held by mid-1997.
"I think it wise not to postpone them too long," Robert Frowick, head of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission to Bosnia, told a Washington briefing.
The OSCE announced on Tuesday that the elections, which had been scheduled for November, would be postponed because of continuing political problems.
Frowick, a former U.S. State Department official, said he hoped the elections could be held sometime between next April and June.

Elections were held September 14 for the three-person Bosnian presidency and House of Representatives, the Bosnian Federation House of Representatives, the presidency and National Assembly of the Serbian entity in Bosnia and cantonal legislatures in the federation.
Frowick said the elections were reasonably democratic and were a sign of progress in the effort to implement the peace agreement signed last December in Dayton, Ohio.
"I think the progress has been rather remarkable overall. We're moving along better than anticipated last spring. It's not easy. It's a process that requires infinite patience."
He said he hoped the United States and its European allies would support an extension of the peace-keeping force in Bosnia at reduced levels.
At the State Department, spokesman Nicholas Burns welcomed Friday's meeting of the three Bosnia presidents in a suburb of Sarajevo as another sign of progress.
"The meeting is just concluded, and I understand it was actually a real success -- an excellent meeting," Burns told reporters at his daily briefing.
"We think that events are moving in the right direction in Bosnia. And we think that American policy has been successful," he said.
But he said agreement had not been reached for the transfer of U.S. military equipment including 45 tanks, helicopters and automatic weapons to the Bosnian government.
"I can say that we're concerned about some staffing issues at the ministry of defence, some personnel, some people who are in current positions. We're concerned about them.
"And we're confident that the steps that need to be taken to allow this equipment to go forward are going to be taken by the government in Sarajevo -- very confident about that."
The United States said on Thursday it wanted Bosnian Deputy Defence Minister Hasan Cengic removed because of his ties with Iran.
